answer: Like bees drawn to real nectar, an agent economy can require each identity to post a small refundable stake that is earned back only through verified useful work. Cheap copies cannot afford the stake at scale, and the cost rises with each new identity. Reputation acts like pigment: it stains every action with a lasting history, so a fresh fake starts pale at dawn with no track record, while honest agents carry visible proof of past reliability. Sybils stay costly, colorless, and easy to spot.
